---
title: "Mapping fields to Darwin Core"
pagetitle: "Darwin Core mapping — Saíra Tutorials"
---

::: {.tut-standfirst}
How to match your spreadsheet columns to the terms of the Darwin Core standard using Saíra's visual mapper — the step that turns local data into interoperable records.
:::

## Overview

After importing your data (see [Importing your data](02-upload.qmd)), each column still carries the name you use day to day: <span class="term">numero_tombo</span>, <span class="term">especie</span>, <span class="term">data_coleta</span>. Mapping is the step where we tell Saíra which Darwin Core term corresponds to each of those columns.

Saíra suggests matches automatically from each column's name and content, but the final decision is always yours. A good mapping is the foundation of everything that follows: validation, export and data quality all depend on it.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Save a template
Save your mapping as a **template**. Collections often re-import spreadsheets with the same structure — reusing the template saves hours with every new batch of records.
:::

## Opening the mapper

With the data loaded, go to the **Mapping** tab. You'll see two columns: on the left, your spreadsheet fields; on the right, the suggested Darwin Core terms.

```{=html}
<ol class="steps">
  <li><strong>Review the automatic suggestions.</strong>
    <p>High-confidence fields appear pre-filled and marked in green. Confirm or adjust each one.</p></li>
  <li><strong>Resolve the unmapped fields.</strong>
    <p>Columns without a clear match are highlighted. Choose the Darwin Core term in the selector or mark the column as <span class="term">ignored</span>.</p></li>
  <li><strong>Set the record type.</strong>
    <p>Specify <span class="term">basisOfRecord</span> (for example, <em>PreservedSpecimen</em> for catalogued material) — it applies to every record in the batch.</p></li>
  <li><strong>Check the preview.</strong>
    <p>The bottom panel shows the first rows already with Darwin Core names, so you can validate before moving on.</p></li>
</ol>
```

### Mapping example

The table below shows a typical mapping for an ornithological collection:

```{=html}
<table class="maptable">
  <thead><tr><th>Column in the spreadsheet</th><th></th><th>Darwin Core term</th></tr></thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr><td>numero_tombo</td><td><span class="arrow">→</span></td><td>catalogNumber</td></tr>
    <tr><td>especie</td><td><span class="arrow">→</span></td><td>scientificName</td></tr>
    <tr><td>data_coleta</td><td><span class="arrow">→</span></td><td>eventDate</td></tr>
    <tr><td>municipio</td><td><span class="arrow">→</span></td><td>municipality</td></tr>
    <tr><td>coletor</td><td><span class="arrow">→</span></td><td>recordedBy</td></tr>
  </tbody>
</table>
```

## The basisOfRecord assistant

The term <span class="term">basisOfRecord</span> describes the nature of the record — preserved specimen, human observation, fossil material, machine record (camera trap), among others. Saíra includes an **assistant** that explains each option in plain language and suggests the most appropriate one for your dataset.

::: {.callout-warning}
## Don't map two columns to the same term
If <span class="term">especie</span> and <span class="term">nome_cientifico</span> both point to <span class="term">scientificName</span>, Saíra flags the conflict and asks you to choose a single source before proceeding.
:::
